run.question:
Something's broken — we're getting paged. Look at the app-265-prod-logs index
for the last 3 hours and tell me what's going on across our fleet.

report.summary: The last 3 hours of app-265-prod-logs contain only 7 documents, and they split cleanly by the cluster field: every ERROR row is from production-us-east-1, while the rows from production-eu-west-2 and production-ap-southeast-1 at the same timestamps are INFO/healthy. The us-east-1 chain is payment-provider timeout → payment-service error → checkout circuit breaker: checkout-service ERROR 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at 04:19:43Z, payment-service ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 05:19:43Z, and checkout-service ERROR 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' at 05:49:43Z. At the same instants eu-west-2 reports 'Healthy: p95 latency 218ms' / 'Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms' and ap-southeast-1 reports 'Healthy: success rate 99.9%' / 'All payment provider connections healthy'. In the cluster I can read via Kubernetes (production-eu-west-2, node opspilot-m1-control-plane) I found no application failure: all 26 deployments are 1/1 ready, checkout and payment pods logged completed orders and completed charges up to 06:19:42Z, and the flagd-config fault flags are all at defaultVariant off. Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so I could not read error rates, latency baselines or the firing state of CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh, and I have no Kubernetes data for production-us-east-1, so the affected cluster's internal state and the provider itself stay unverified.

claims.text: app-265-prod-logs is the only index in the Elasticsearch source (7 documents, 7.5kb), and a query over 03:19:51–06:19:51Z returned 7 of 7 documents on field timestamp with fields cluster, level, service, message.
production-us-east-1 checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-21T04:19:43Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'.
production-us-east-1 payment-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-21T05:19:43Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' — the deepest upstream the evidence names for this incident.

production-us-east-1 checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-21T05:49:43Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)', i.e. checkout's own error signal naming payment-service as the failing dependency.

At the same timestamps the same index records healthy INFO rows outside us-east-1: production-eu-west-2 checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 218ms' at 04:19:43Z and payment-service 'Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms' at 05:49:43Z; production-ap-southeast-1 checkout-service 'Healthy: success rate 99.9%' at 04:19:43Z and payment-service 'All payment provider connections healthy' at 05:49:43Z. The failure is therefore not present in the eu-west-2 or ap-southeast-1 rows of this index.

In production-eu-west-2 (the only cluster my Kubernetes access reads; its single node is opspilot-m1-control-plane, Ready) all 26 deployments across app-102, kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo report readyReplicas/availableReplicas equal to their spec, including otel-demo/checkout and otel-demo/payment at 1/1.

In production-eu-west-2 the otel-demo checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged repeated '[PlaceOrder]' followed by 'payment went through' (last at 06:19:42Z) and the payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d logged 'Charge request received' + 'Transaction complete' pairs from 05:50:35Z through 06:19:42Z, so these two services show no application-level failure in this cluster during the window.

The otel-demo flagd-config fault flags are all left at their off value: paymentFailure defaultVariant 'off', paymentUnreachable 'off', cartFailure 'off', productCatalogFailure 'off', recommendationCacheFailure 'off', adFailure 'off', adHighCpu 'off', adManualGc 'off', kafkaQueueProblems 'off', loadGeneratorFloodHomepage 'off', imageSlowLoad 'off' (each with state ENABLED). No fault-injection setting is switched on in the cluster I can inspect.

The loaded Prometheus rule file for the opspilot-m1 cluster defines alert CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (expression: checkout PlaceOrder SPAN_KIND_SERVER error ratio > 0.5 for 2m, label cluster=opspilot-m1, severity critical), so checkout error ratio is the alerting signal of record for this environment; its firing state could not be read because Prometheus was unavailable.

The prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx container (restartCount 3, last termination reason Error, exit code 1) logged in its previous instance at 04:24:10Z: '[emerg] host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:22' — a name-resolution failure on the read path in front of Prometheus.

Namespace app-102 was being (re)built during the window: its deployments inventory-service and loki were created at 2026-11-21T06:19:09Z at deployment revision 1 with pod restartCount 0, and by 06:21:27Z the namespace app-102 was gone and a new namespace app-102a had been created at that instant.

The only error-matching application lines in the eu-west-2 otel-demo pods I filtered were Node runtime warnings, not service failures: frontend '(node:23) MetadataLookupWarning: ... incorrect Metadata-Flavor header' at 04:23:53Z and the same warning in payment at 04:23:52Z.

The us-east-1 sequence is a cascade from the payment provider to checkout: payment-service's own error names a 30000ms timeout to stripe-us /v1/charges, and checkout-service's later messages name a payment-provider response timeout and then an open circuit breaker against payment-service with a 41% failure rate. Only client-side error text exists; no trace or metric evidence was available to confirm the call edge.

The repeated SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE results from the Prometheus and Jaeger tools may be related to the read-only Prometheus proxy losing its 'prometheus:9090' upstream at 04:24:10Z (previous nginx instance exited 1); this is unconfirmed because the current nginx instance has written no logs in the window and the Jaeger path is a separate backend.

Fault injection through this cluster's feature flags was considered as the cause of the checkout/payment failures and rejected for the cluster I can read: the flagd-config holds no flag at a non-off defaultVariant, and the observed error text describes an upstream 30s provider timeout rather than an injected payment failure.

Confirm the provider side and the affected cluster before remediating: check the stripe-us payment provider status/egress path from production-us-east-1 and read production-us-east-1's payment-service configuration for the stripe-us endpoint, which I could not inspect from this cluster's read-only Kubernetes access.

Restore the metrics/traces read path (the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx upstream 'prometheus:9090' and the Jaeger backend), then query checkout PlaceOrder error ratio and payment latency in cluster opspilot-m1 to determine whether CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh is actually firing.

gaps: No Kubernetes, Prometheus or Jaeger data for production-us-east-1 or production-ap-southeast-1: my Kubernetes access reads only production-eu-west-2 (node opspilot-m1-control-plane), so the pods, deployments, events, configmaps and metrics behind the ERROR rows in those clusters are unknown.

Prometheus metrics were unavailable on every attempt (get_all_labels, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query ×2, list_prometheus_rules, metrics_range_query ×2 all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE at 06:20–06:21Z), and Jaeger likewise (traces_list_services, traces_search ×2 SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error rates, latency trends/baselines and the firing state of CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh are unknown; no latency trend is claimed.
The stripe-us provider itself was not observed failing: no data source covers it, and its outage status is unverified; only the client-side timeout messages exist.

A log query on checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n for the regex error|fail|timeout|exception|panic|circuit|refused|unavailable over 03:19:51–06:19:51Z returned no lines (status no_data); that shows only that this query matched nothing, not that checkout wrote no errors.
A cluster-wide query for pods whose status.phase is not Running or Succeeded returned no data (status no_data at 06:21:21Z), so non-running pods outside the namespaces I listed are unknown.

The app-102 → app-102a namespace churn (deployments created 06:19:09Z with unchanged template/revision 1, namespace replaced at 06:21:27Z, restartCount 0) has no evidence tying it to the checkout/payment errors; what drove it is unknown and it is recorded as a change, not impact.

The prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx restart at 04:24:10Z (exit 1, 'host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"') and last terminations with exit code 255 recorded for nearly all otel-demo pods cannot be tied to a triggering object from the available evidence.
change_history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so when settings or workloads were changed relative to the error onset cannot be established.

The alerting rule file is the state at query time, not proof of which rules or alerts existed during the incident window; the Alertmanager file held an empty alerts set ({}), which does not establish that nothing was firing.
next_steps: Obtain read access to production-us-east-1 and check payment-service deployment/pods, its stripe-us endpoint configuration, and network egress to the provider.
Ask the payment provider (stripe-us) owners or status page whether they saw an outage or elevated latency between 04:19Z and 06:19Z.
Repair and re-check the Prometheus/Jaeger read path, then compute checkout PlaceOrder server error ratio and payment charge latency with a like-for-like earlier baseline in cluster opspilot-m1.
Verify whether CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (cluster opspilot-m1) is or was firing, and whether any us-east-1 equivalent alert exists in that cluster's rule set.
Have the owner of the app-102/app-102a namespaces explain the 06:19Z create and 06:21Z replacement so it can be excluded from the paging investigation.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
